status: Surface attachment, inherited interface identities and system-memory overlay rules implemented; all applicable original Wine conformance still incomplete.
changes: System-memory overlay allocation returns DDERR_NOOVERLAYHW without allocation; incompatible SYS|VID placement remains the earlier INVALIDCAPS error.

Depth attachments require matching dimensions and keep the caller namespace separately from the actually held target public interface. Duplicate same-view attachment returns SURFACEALREADYATTACHED, foreign-view duplicate CANNOTATTACHSURFACE, and foreign-view delete SURFACENOTATTACHED without mutation. Matching delete releases the saved held group and clears metadata before target rebind. Retiring one public group does not detach while the allocation remains live.
Inherited Surface2/3 GetAttachedSurface and EnumAttachedSurfaces return Surface1 and increment its public reference group. Surface4/7 retain their respective public interfaces.

Draw4-created manual flip attachments are accepted like legacy Draw1; Surface7 still permits only depth attachment. Inserting before a backbuffer transfers the BACKBUFFER role. Immediate flip-edge querying replaces whole-ring searching; direct reverse-primary edges remain valid. XP additional successor reference when removing a manual member before an implicit buffer is preserved and explicitly retired by the conformance sequence.

XP preparation identifies actual button captions and uses property-sheet cancellation rather than assuming an IDCANCEL lookup is the correct control. Restart requests are matched by body and No caption/ID. PnP queue status must remain idle before launch; a read-only postcheck rejects later system UI. Only a complete execution explicitly rejected by that environment check can be repeated once in the same RAM VM; both raw execution logs remain, and a clean-environment assertion failure does not trigger rerun. Startup marker and flushed preparation logs prevent missed-launch fallback from spawning another preparation process. All setup ends before the original test and postcheck runs only after it.
